_note: vCAOC IFF/SIF code plan. Codes are 4-digit (Mode 2, Mode 3/A) or 2-digit (Mode 1) octal. Real Mode 1 assignments are theater/ATO specific and not public: the Mode 1 table here is the vCAOC's own scheme. Reserved Mode 3/A codes follow the FAA AIM 4-1-20 and ICAO practice.

reserved.use: Entering SSR airspace without an assigned code (ICAO)
Military in restricted / warning areas when no other code is assigned (US)
Emergency series (special indicators); 7777 never used by civil aircraft

mode3._note: A line's Mode 3/A block is its Mode 1 code: SEAD (Mode 1 30) flies 3011-3017, 3021-3027 and so on. Slot C of block BB covers BBC1-BBC7; the flight lead squawks BBC1 and the last member of a non-standard flight squawks BBC1 + (n - 1), as in NELLISAFBI 11-250 §4.3.2 (lead 6411, #4 6414); all others squawk standby. Slot 0 is never used, so nothing ends in 00. A slot holding any reserved code is skipped (block 12 loses 120, 125 and 127). When a block is full the line takes a spare Mode 1 code of the same family, and its block. Mode 3/A starts with Mode 1 because the F-16C sends its first two code wheels as Mode 1.

mode1._note: First digit = mission family, second digit (0-3) = sub-role. Optional daily rotation adds the ATO day to the second digit (mod 4).

mode2._note: Optional, per airframe: first two digits = the registered group's number (octal), last two = aircraft in the group (01-77). Only modules with a full IFF use it (Heatblur F-14 / F-4E / Viggen, F-15E).

mode4.default: Mode 4 ON. Code A until 0000Z, then code B. In DCS most aircraft answer friend/foe by coalition, so this is discipline and realism, not separation.
mode4.procedures: Mode 3/C and Mode 4 on from takeoff to landing. Flight lead squawks the ATO Mode 3; the last member of a non-standard flight squawks the ATO last-member code; all others standby. Mode 1 per the ATO mission line (always the first two digits of the Mode 3/A code). F-16C: IFF enable switch M1/M3 and dial the Mode 3/A code on the four wheels; the first two wheels are Mode 1. Squawk 7600 lost comms, 7700 emergency. Mode S flight ID = ATO callsign where the aircraft supports it. Turn IFF off only in published IFF-off areas.

rules: On range: all aircraft squawk Mode C and a tactical Mode 3 — never 1200 (AFMAN 13-212V1 NTTR Add A §3.1.3).
Lead squawks the assigned discrete Mode 3/C; the last member of a non-standard flight squawks lead + n; others standby (NELLISAFBI 11-250 §4.3.2).
Into the NAS: last member squawks the lead's first two digits + 00 (NELLISAFBI 11-250 §4.3.3).
IFF-off operations only when authorized through NTTR scheduling, in the NTTR IFF-off area (AFMAN 13-212V1 NTTR Add A Att 16).
